findings_and_connected_questions.first_failed_contract: An admitted finite prism passed to a native convex-mesh operation should have finite recentered vertices, or the owner should explicitly reject an unrepresentable conversion before the native handoff.
findings_and_connected_questions.static_reasoning: Let M=f32::MAX and use six abstract points in metres: top [(0,M,0),(1,0,0),(0,0,1)] and paired base [(0,-M,0),(1,-M,0),(0,0,1)]. Each component is finite, X/Z pairs match, all top Y are at least base Y and two heights are positive. Under the inspected lock-matched glam scalar Vec3 sum and ordinary IEEE f32 operations in the displayed source order, y accumulation is M, M, M, 0, -M, -M, so the prism sum is finite. The X/Z triangle has positive exact area. The two collider implementations divide this finite sum by six, then subtract the resulting center from every f32 point. The first y subtraction is M - (-M/6), which overflows to +infinity under ordinary rounding; the source passes the resulting vertex vector to SharedShape::convex_mesh without a new finite check. For a valid nonzero property and admitted members, from_prisms builds and validates canonical topology for this one cell and no cut faces; the scene- and gate-relative Position constructors admit individual finite values. For the boundary mesh path, matching element/binding and any enclosing wire/producer gates remain separate conditions.
findings_and_connected_questions.limits: This is symbolic source reasoning, not a constructed prism, evaluated f32 probe, fixture, deserialization, native mesh or product run. The locked glam scalar implementation and ordinary rounding assumptions are shown, but selected features, target/compiler FP behavior, complete supported producer range, native Parry requirements/outcomes, full boundary binding and product effects are not established. Native convex_mesh may reject or otherwise handle the input; no panic, malformed installed collider or actual bad scene is asserted.
